P-08 Ticket generation request

Bangla name: টিকিট জেনারেশন অনুরোধ

← 20 · User portal · Contents · Open queries

1. Name and purpose

Ticket generation request. After payment the customer holds a Paid order and draft ticket rows. When the event's ticket availability date arrives, the customer presses Request tickets; the platform then prints a blank PDF per ticket, has each one digitally signed with a QR code by the TSP, and the order turns Requested and later Generated. The customer waits on the page (it re-checks every 30 seconds) until the signed PDFs can be downloaded (P-09).

2. Trigger and actor

Signed-in customer on /{lang}/tickets/ticket-details/{publicId} (TicketPreviewComponent), only when the order is Paid and the event's ticketAvailabilityStartDateTime has passed (holder names and phones are filled in beforehand, P-09).

3. Business flow

  1. Before the availability date the button is inactive. From the availability date on, Request tickets opens a confirmation pop-up ("Once generated, the ticket details cannot be changed"; the pop-up text is hard-coded in English, not translated).
  2. After confirmation the order status becomes Requested; a pop-up says generation is in progress; the page shows the "in progress" state and re-checks every 30 seconds.
  3. When every ticket is signed the order becomes Generated (S-06); the page reloads the tickets and shows the Download, Share and, for more than one ticket, Download all buttons.

4. Technical flow

  1. Draft tickets exist because the details call creates them on demand: GetTicketsInfo creates the rows of a Paid order that has none (InitiateBulkTicketForNewlyPaidOrder, under the Redis lock create_user_ticket_{publicId}), in addition to the payment callback and the worker (S-07).
  2. [HTTP, no token → Ticketing] The portal sends PATCH {services.tickets}/ticketing/api/v1/booking-order-ticket/generate-request/{publicId} with an empty body (BookingApiService.requestTicketsById). The controller action has no [Authorize] and the manager does not check the caller; the portal's token interceptor still attaches the user token because the URL contains /ticketing.
  3. TicketManager.TicketGenerateRequest:
  4. reads the order from Booking ([HTTP, no token] GET .../user-booking-order/public-id/{id});
  5. ValidateTicketGeneration: status Requested or Generated → Request to generate ticket is already taken.; not Paid → Only paid order requests can generate tickets; the event's TicketAvailabilityStartDateTime later than now (UTC) → You can request after ticket availability date.;
  6. loads the level info and the published ticket layout of the program, venue and gallery (A-13);
  7. for each ticket, draws the blank PDF (GetBlankPdf) and uploads it to the ticket bucket under {BlankBase}/user/{userId}/{orderId}/{ticketNumber}.pdf (X-20); sets the ticket status Requested and the layout's back-page URL; saves;
  8. for each ticket publishes [SQS: TicketSigning] a SignedTicketGeneration message (UnsignedTicketUrl, QRPosition by layout size, GateId = the level's entry gate, Data = name, phone, date and time (UTC+6), ticket id, event id, gallery, block, level, entry gate, mini gate, seat); the signing worker is S-08;
  9. [HTTP, no token → Booking] PATCH .../user-booking-order/generate-ticket-request/{publicId} sets the order status Requested, and returns the order with its tickets.
  10. The browser updates the ticket statuses and the order status from the response and opens the "generation" pop-up. From now on ngOnInit's timer (every 30 s) calls [HTTP + user token] GET /booking/api/v1/user-booking-order/check-generated-status?id= while the status is Requested; when it returns true the portal reloads the tickets (details).
  11. Background: S-08 signs and stores each ticket (SignedTicketUrl); S-06 marks the order Generated when all its tickets are signed; S-12 sends the push message.

7. Data and side effects

Blank PDFs in the ticket bucket, ticket and order status changes, one SQS message per ticket, later signed PDFs and a push notification.

9. Handover notes

  1. Anyone can trigger generation for any order whose public id they know: the Ticketing action and the Booking generate-ticket-request action are anonymous (X-18, S-07 note 4). The availability-date and Paid checks still apply.
  2. Order of the writes is not atomic. Tickets are marked Requested and messages are published before the Booking order is set to Requested; if the Booking call fails the tickets are already being signed while the order still shows Paid, and pressing the button again is refused (ValidateTicketGeneration looks at the order, which is still Paid, so a second request re-prints and re-publishes) [UNCONFIRMED: Q-40].
  3. Holder data is frozen at request time. The QR payload contains the name and phone as stored when the request is made; editing is refused afterwards because the order is no longer Paid (P-09).
  4. Availability time uses two clocks. The button is enabled by the browser's clock (Date.now() against ticketAvailabilityStartDateTime, refreshed every 30 s) while the server compares with UTC now; a wrong device clock can show the button early (server refuses) or late.
  5. Request time is the TSP's busiest moment. When the availability date arrives many customers press the button together; the work is queued in TicketSigning and signed by the worker (S-08); the customer only waits and polls.
  6. No timeout on the waiting state. If signing stalls, the order stays Requested and the page keeps polling for ever; support finds it in the issue list or reconciliation (A-23) [UNCONFIRMED: Q-12].
  7. Layout is read at request time. A layout published later does not affect tickets already requested (A-13).

11. Developer test guide

Local testability: Partial. Signing needs the TSP certificate, which is a dummy locally, so tickets reach Requested but are not signed.
